clue.text: Improving colt starts to come on form for the big race

indicators.note: to come on means to follow on after, so these letters go after the previous piece

parts.note: form means class, as in a school class or year group

indicators.note: starts means the first letters of the words Improving and colt are taken

explanation.surface: A young horse is getting better and shaping up for a major race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like racing form but is a school class; 'starts' and 'to come on' do the rest. The Classics are five major British flat races, such as the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: The Classics are the five chief British flat races, so a Classic is a big race.

clue.text: Shy embraces, with German courtesy

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: coy means shy
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A bashful person hugging a German, out of politeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' signals the container; 'with German' is read as one unit, the German word for with.
explanation.definitionFit: Comity is mutual civility and consideration, as between nations.

clue.text: Obliquely request a new diocesan centre

parts.note: ask means request

indicators.note: centre means the middle letters of the word diocesan

explanation.surface: Asking, at an angle, for a fresh hub for the diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes CE, the middle two letters of diocesan.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to look sideways, so it means at a slant.

clue.text: The point at which to take a short break

definitions.text: The point at which to take a short break

parts.words: The point at which to take a short break
parts.note: a punctuation point marking a pause longer than a comma but shorter than a full stop

explanation.surface: The right moment to stop briefly for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like a moment in time, but it is a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This mark signals a pause in a sentence, a brief stop in reading.

clue.text: Book for amateur sportsmen

explanation.surface: A book written for amateur athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: Corinthians are two epistles in the New Testament; Corinthian is also an old word for a gentleman amateur in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's letters to the church at Corinth are a Bible book, and Corinthian once meant a wealthy amateur athlete.

clue.text: Tale of previously unknown city

parts.note: novel means new, never seen before
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A story about a city nobody had heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: A short prose story, longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.

clue.text: No sound heard from an Arab perhaps

indicators.note: sound heard means the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse, and a horse neighs

explanation.surface: An Arabian stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' looks like a person but is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nay is an old word for no, a refusal.

clue.text: This general could assist metropolitan girl with vehicle

parts.note: Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An army general could help a city girl who has a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A vicar general assists a bishop; a metropolitan is an archbishop, not someone from a city. 'General' looks like a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar general is a church officer deputising for a bishop or archbishop.

clue.text: Player requiring much time on stage

parts.note: long means a lot of time
a leg is a stage of a journey

explanation.surface: An actor who needs a long time on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' and 'stage' suggest an actor; LONG LEG is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman near the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Long leg is a cricket fielding position, so the name stands for the fielder there.

clue.text: Jung and Freud for example, were surprised by female leanings, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the words are pronounced the same as the entry

parts.note: Anna is a female name and lists are leanings or tilts, as of a ship

explanation.surface: Two famous psychologists were taken aback by a woman's tendencies.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNA LISTS sounds like the answer; 'were surprised by' is padding for the surface. A list is a ship's lean to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Jung and Freud practised psychoanalysis, so they are examples of mind doctors.

clue.text: Manage to attend drunken revel

parts.note: to make a meeting is to manage to get to it
merry is a mild word for tipsy

explanation.surface: Someone who manages to turn up at a boozy party.
explanation.definitionFit: To make merry is to celebrate with feasting and drinking, which is what reveling means.

clue.text: Scots aren't capable of producing a tropical plant

explanation.surface: Scottish people cannot grow a certain tropical plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed count (3) is a misprint for (5).
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect 'canna' means cannot; a canna is also a lily-like flowering plant from the tropics.

clue.text: Unconventional cut in coat

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so the letters of cut in are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coat with an unusual cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose garment or a close-fitting military jacket, a kind of coat.

clue.text: Teachers meeting to accept head in election without fear or favour

indicators.note: to accept means to take inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

indicators.note: head in means the first letter of the word election

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Teachers at a conference must take on a leader impartially at the ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head in' picks the first letter of election and 'to accept' puts it inside, just after the first letter. The National Union of Teachers is a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting impartially, taking no side, is acting without fear or favour.

clue.text: Easily satisfied requirement accepted by a French king when guillotined

indicators.note: accepted by means held inside, so one piece goes within the others

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: guillotined means beheaded, so the first letter of king is cut off

parts.note: taken as written
a demand is a requirement

explanation.surface: A French king beheaded in the Revolution had a modest demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when guillotined' beheads the king, and 'accepted by' places the requirement inside the French article plus what is left of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undemanding asks little, so is content with little.

clue.text: Find it hard to raise the wind after a touch?

definitions.text: Find it hard to raise the wind after a touch?

parts.words: Find it hard to raise the wind after a touch?
parts.note: raising the wind is British slang for finding money; someone touched for a loan then sees their funds run short, while the phrase also suggests sensing a cold current of air

explanation.surface: Struggling to get the breeze going after a light contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise the wind' is old British slang for getting money together, and a 'touch' is a request for a loan; the answer means to suffer from a lack of money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be short of cash, which is what finding it hard to raise money amounts to.

clue.text: Surprise attack by a doctor on a nasty bit of work in practice

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: use means custom or practice
a cad is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A doctor's surgery hit by a sudden assault from a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CAD inside USE. MB, a British medical degree, stands for doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambuscade is an ambush, an attack launched from hiding.

clue.text: Unlucky injury sustained swallowing a sort of bone

parts.note: ill means harm or injury

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fed means sustained or nourished
a T-bone is a kind of steak bone

explanation.surface: An unfortunate injury from swallowing a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts A and T inside FED, making FATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-fated means doomed to misfortune, so unfortunate.

clue.text: A land one possible associates with moving aria

indicators.note: possible suggests one potential arrangement among several, so the letters of A land one are rearranged

parts.note: mobile means moving

explanation.surface: A country that one might link with a stirring song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges A LAND ONE into LA DONNA E; 'associates with' just joins it to MOBILE. The aria is the Duke's song from Verdi's Rigoletto.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous tenor song from Verdi's opera Rigoletto, an operatic solo.

clue.text: Lowest river vermin

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
a pest is vermin

explanation.surface: The most despicable rats by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest means furthest down, so lowest in depth.

clue.text: Let nine off — that's merciful

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so the letters of let nine are rearranged

explanation.surface: Letting nine people go free is kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means tolerant and forgiving, inclined to mercy.

clue.text: Publication bar over subject of St 'Stephen, possibly

parts.note: mag is short for magazine

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a ray is a bar or beam of light

explanation.surface: A magazine bans an article about a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RAY into YAR. St Stephen was the first King of Hungary, so a Hungarian was his subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A Magyar is a Hungarian, and Stephen I ruled Hungary.

clue.text: Strange forenames for a brother

indicators.note: strange means odd or unusual, so the letters of forenames are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peculiar first names for a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Masonic order call each other brother, so a brother is a member of that society.

clue.text: Broadcast aimed for radio and television

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of aimed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A programme aimed at radio and television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the scene but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio and television are mass communication outlets, together called the media.

clue.text: Annual visitor in pleasant accommodation

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words pleasant accommodation

explanation.surface: A yearly guest staying in nice lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas comes once a year, at Christmas, so he is a visitor every year.

clue.text: It's the fashion for Harrow to follow ageless Eton

indicators.note: to follow means this piece comes after the previous one
ageless means without an age, here a synonym for age (eon) taken out of the word Eton

parts.note: to harrow is to distress or tear, as does to rend

explanation.surface: Harrow copying Eton is the latest craze, both being famous English public schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ageless' removes a synonym for an age (EON) from Eton, leaving one letter; 'to follow' adds the rest. Harrow and Eton look like the rival English schools but are just words here.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is the current style or vogue, what is fashionable now.

clue.text: Old letter recently found in frank collection

parts.note: phi is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet
lately means recently

explanation.surface: An old letter turns up among a candid set of papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frank' looks like an adjective meaning candid, but here it is the postmark that franks a stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp collecting gathers franked postage stamps, so it is a collection of franks.

clue.text: Apposite to some extent but not right

indicators.note: not means the letter is removed

parts.note: in part means to some extent

explanation.surface: Only partly relevant, and not correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R from PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat means timely and fitting, as in a pat reply.

clue.text: Carried back starter from Tandoori take-away

indicators.note: back means the word for carried is written backwards

parts.note: carted means carried

indicators.note: starter from means the first letter of the word Tandoori

explanation.surface: Someone carried home the first course of an Indian takeaway meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CARTED into DETRAC; 'starter from' adds T. 'Take-away' and 'Tandoori' paint a meal, but the definition is the verb 'take away'.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to diminish or remove some value from, that is to subtract.

clue.text: He cries "Hello", perhaps

parts.note: someone who says hello to arriving guests welcomes them; in Scots to greet also means to weep, so he cries in two senses

explanation.surface: A man calls out a welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots 'greet' means to weep, so the cries may be tears as well as a welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who welcomes visitors at a door calls out a salutation to them.
